title: 浣溪沙（山下兰芽短浸溪）
titleEn: Silk-Washing Stream (“Below the hill, short orchid shoots dip into the brook”)
author: 苏轼
intro: Rivers in China flow east — but beside this temple the stream runs west. Seeing it, the exiled Su Shi decides that growing old need not mean giving up.
analysis: 词前有小序：游蕲水的清泉寺，寺在兰溪边，溪水向西流。上阕写景：山脚下，兰草的嫩芽短短的，浸在溪水里；松林间的沙路干干净净，没有泥；傍晚下着细雨，杜鹃鸟在啼叫。画面清新，但“暮雨”“子规啼”也带一点淡淡的愁。下阕转为议论：谁说人生不能再回到少年？你看门前的流水还能向西流！不要因为头发白了，就唱“黄鸡催晓”那样感叹时光流逝的歌。中国的河大多向东流，古人常用“东流水”比喻时光一去不回；苏轼看到一条向西流的溪水，就从中看到希望。当时他被贬黄州，又生着病，却写出这样乐观的句子，表现了他热爱生活、不服老的态度。
analysisEn: The preface sets the scene: Su Shi visited Clear Spring Temple in Qishui, beside Orchid Brook, whose water flows west. The first half is pure landscape. Short new orchid shoots dip into the stream at the foot of the hill; the sandy path through the pines is clean, without a speck of mud; evening rain patters down while a cuckoo calls. It is fresh and quiet, though evening rain and the cuckoo’s cry carry a hint of sadness. The second half turns to thought. Who says we can never be young again? Look — the water outside the gate can still flow west! So don’t sing that sad old song about the yellow rooster crowing the hours away just because your hair is white. Most Chinese rivers flow east to the sea, and poets had long used “water flowing east” as a picture of time that never returns. A stream running the other way gives Su Shi a reason for hope. He was in exile and had just been ill, yet he wrote these cheerful lines. They show his love of life and his refusal to feel old.
background: Su Shi (1037–1101), also called Su Dongpo, wrote this in the spring of 1082 during his exile in Huangzhou. He had gone to nearby Qishui to see a doctor, Pang Anchang, and the two visited Clear Spring Temple together.
pronunciation: 少 shào（再少：再回到少年）；子规 zǐ guī；萧萧 xiāo xiāo。小序中的“蕲水”读 qí shuǐ。
version: 采用通行版本。原有小序：“游蕲水清泉寺，寺临兰溪，溪水西流。”网站只收词。苏轼《游沙湖》一文也记此词，作“君看流水尚能西”，通行本作“门前流水尚能西”。“唱黄鸡”化用白居易《醉歌》“黄鸡催晓丑时鸣”。

lines.py: shān xià lán yá duǎn jìn xī
lines.lit: Below the hill, orchid shoots, short, soak in the brook;
lines.en: At the hill’s foot, short orchid shoots dip into the stream;

lines.py: sōng jiān shā lù jìng wú ní
lines.lit: among the pines, the sandy road is clean, without mud;
lines.en: the sandy path through the pines is clean, not a speck of mud;

lines.py: xiāo xiāo mù yǔ zǐ guī tí
lines.lit: pattering evening rain; the cuckoo cries.
lines.en: evening rain whispers down, and a cuckoo calls.

lines.py: shuí dào rén shēng wú zài shào
lines.lit: Who says in life there is no being young again?
lines.en: Who says we can never be young again?

lines.py: mén qián liú shuǐ shàng néng xī
lines.lit: The flowing water before the gate can still go west!
lines.en: Look, the stream outside the gate still runs west!

lines.py: xiū jiāng bái fà chàng huáng jī
lines.lit: Don’t, because of white hair, sing of the yellow rooster.
lines.en: White hair is no reason to sing the rooster’s sad song of passing time.

words.note: 就是杜鹃鸟，叫声凄切，古诗里常带愁思。
读 shào，如“少年”“老少”；不是 shǎo。
现代汉语书面语“尚未”“尚且”；口语说“还”。

words.en: to sing of the yellow rooster — to lament passing time
words.note: 典故：白居易诗说黄鸡报晓、日落催年，感叹人老得快。

imagery.name: 兰
imagery.zh: 溪边新长的兰芽，带来春天的清新和生机。
imagery.en: New orchid shoots by the brook bring spring freshness and life.

imagery.name: 松
imagery.zh: 松林间干净的沙路，写出环境的幽静清洁。
imagery.en: The clean path through the pines makes the place feel calm and pure.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 流水本来象征时光一去不回，这里的溪水却向西流，变成了“青春可以再来”的希望。
imagery.en: Flowing water usually means time lost forever; this stream runs west, so it becomes a sign that youth can return.

imagery.name: 白发
imagery.zh: 白发代表年老，诗人劝人不要因为老了就悲观。
imagery.en: White hair means age — and the poet says it is no reason for gloom.
